Q: "uv run" can't find module in venv even though it is installed after first run A:

uv run may skip the sync step if uv thingks the env is already up to date.

Quick Fix:

  1. Bypass the sync entirely:

    uv run --no-sync python experiments/experiment_hello.py

  2. Use frozen mode

    uv run --frozen python experiments/experiment_hello.py

Long Term Fix: Switch to Hatchling:

[build-system] 
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "testing-installed-package"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = []

[project.scripts]
testing-installed-package = "testing_installed_package:main"

Then:

rm -rf .venv uv.lock
uv sync

This should permanently fix the issue: hatchling handles editable installs more reliably.

Q: Include only certain file types when searching in Visual Studio A:

This question needs to be revisited with the newer versions of VS (2026 for this post). I don't like their co-pilot find feature and the older find function does not allow to select file types in the project. Instead you have to use regular expressions ☹️

When using CTRL+SHFT+F, in VS 2026, this is what you see. And if you click the settings button it allows you to add more Exclusion filters. The older version where you just select file types to be searched is much simpler (IMO) and now it's not (I believe this is because they want you to use AI for everything.)

So now I use an old GrepWin tool to find what I want quickly. Thanks to Stefan's Tools.

Q: How to obtain a table from an online pdf in R A:

Start off with the FACT most modern PDF are text with compressed contents so non viewable without a PDF designed decompressor (PDF RENDER ENGINE) this could be your browser with a local plug-in such as Chromes PDFium but NOTE IT IS USING LOCAL CPU on a DOWNLOAD inside the browser not the server. Thus, no such thing as view a remote pdf nor extract content of a remote pdf unless the SERVER IS A PDF EXTRACTOR like ADOBE SAAS.

Q: Efficient algorithm for pixel neighborhood difference in OpenCV A:

I'm too many years late, but I'd like to contribute. Instead of nested for loops, you could define 8 filters, each one corresponding to the difference between the center pixel and one neighbour.

Something like this (I'm using Python):

import numpy as np

filters = []
for i in range(9):
    f = np.zeros(9, dtype=float)
    # You skip index 4 because it corresponds to the center pixel
    if i != 4:
        f[i] = -1
        f[4] = 1
        f = f.reshape((3, 3))
        filters.append(f)

For example, the first filter will be:

f = [[-1, 0, 0],
    [0, 1, 0],
    [0, 0, 0]]

Then, you simply have to filter the image with the 8 filters and take the absolute values:

diffs = np.stack([cv2.filter2D(x_gray, -1, f) for f in self.filters])
diffs = np.abs(diffs).sum(axis=0)

Just in case anyone is interested, I have implemented this already (see this repo)
